learning_objective: 🎯 Become a landscape reader! Learn how rivers, groundwater, glaciers, wind, and waves carve out amazing shapes in nature over millions of years.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Rivers are the most powerful geomorphic agents. In their youth (mountains), they cause heavy downward erosion forming V-shaped valleys and waterfalls. In their old age (plains), they deposit sediments forming floodplains and deltas.

In areas with limestone rocks, acidic rainwater seeps underground and dissolves the rock. This creates unique 'Karst' landforms like sinkholes, underground caves, and hanging pillars called stalactites and stalagmites.
Glaciers are slow-moving rivers of ice. They carve out U-shaped valleys and deep armchair-like depressions called Cirques. When they melt, they drop massive piles of debris called Moraines.

In deserts, wind creates mushroom rocks by eroding bases, and deposits sand to form Sand Dunes. On coasts, powerful ocean waves crash against rocks to form sea cliffs, sea arches, and eventually deposit sand to form beaches.

fun_activity.title: 🏝️ The Sandbox Delta
fun_activity.instructions: Make a small pile of loose sand or dirt. Slowly pour water from a cup over the top. Watch how the water cuts a path (valley) and carries the sand down to the bottom, fanning out into a triangle shape. You just created a miniature River Delta!

exam_tips: 📌 Always associate V-shaped valleys with Running Water (Rivers) and U-shaped valleys with Glaciers.
📌 Stalactites hang tightly from the ceiling ('c' for ceiling), while Stalagmites grow mightily from the ground ('g' for ground).
📌 Distinguish clearly between Erosional landforms (like Cirques, Gorges, Sea cliffs) and Depositional landforms (like Deltas, Moraines, Beaches).
quick_recap: ⭐ Landscapes evolve through distinct stages: Youth, Mature, and Old stage.
⭐ Running water is the most dominant geomorphic agent on Earth.
⭐ Every geomorphic agent creates specific erosional features and specific depositional features.
